parties:
Sree Sree Narayan Chakra Bigraha ------ Petitioner
Vs.
Niranjan Bhattacharjee ----- Opposite Party
full_judgment: 10. The plaintiff, in view of a recital in the will, claims that Brajahari was indifferent and callous type of man and as such he was not appointed executor though he was the eldest son of Banga Chandra. It appears to me that the question whether Brojahari was indifferent or callous type of man or a normal man is not very much relevant for the purpose of arriving at a decision in this suit. The relevant question is whether Brojahari left the homestead of his father or used to reside on that homestead. The will executed on 3rd Chaitra, 1284 Maghi era which corresponds to 1924 A.D. There is no evidence to show in which year Banga Chandra died except the statement of D.W.1 as referred to earlier. Now, from exhibits 6 and 6(a) it appears that the property was recorded in R.S. Khatians in the names of three sons of Banga Chandra in equal shares and not in the names of the deity. These khatiana were finally published in the year 1930. The plaintiff did not claim that the khatians were wrong. That means these khatians remained unchallenged. In these khatinas 3/1rd shares has been recorded in the name of Brojahari and as such it cannot be said that Brojahari left the locality. The D.W.1 in his cross-examination said that the marriage ceremony of Brojahari was held in his father's house. P.W. 5 who is 75 years old stated that Brojahari was known to him and he used to reside in the suit homestead and also died there. This is exactly the case of the contesting defendant. It is definite case of the contesting defendent that his father used to reside in the suit homestead and died there. In view of R.S. khatians and the statements of the P.W.1 and P.W. 5 as mentioned above it is quite clear the Brojahari used to reside in the homestead plot of his father till his death. So, there is no truth in the claim of the plaintiff that Brojahari had no right to enjoy the proshadi in view of the condition laid down in the will because he did not reside in the homestead of Banga Chandra.
